claude.rationale: This was a whole-company reverse triangular merger in which VWR's laboratory- and production-products distribution business (T4) and its operating distribution processes (T5) crossed the ownership boundary together as a going concern, with VWR surviving as a wholly-owned subsidiary — product and process moved as one, so gap_45 = 0. However, at the T5/T6 boundary the deal transferred the operational business while management participation was "expressly not a condition," only the CFO had a disclosed continued-employment arrangement, no equity rollover was required, and certain directors resigned effective the Closing Date — a documented process-vs-people/management mismatch, so gap_56 = 1. That gap was contractually cushioned via merger-agreement provisions requiring continuing employees be provided no-less-favorable compensation and benefits in the aggregate for a specified post-closing period, so gap_mitigated = yes; T1 coded replace because the New Mountain/Avantor principal was installed and prior management/controlling intent exited.

grok.rationale: The deal was a whole-company reverse triangular merger in which VWR survived intact as Avantor’s wholly-owned subsidiary, so VWR’s customer-facing distribution products/services (T4) and the operating business that produced them (T5) crossed together with no product-vs-process split documented at closing. T6 moved only partially—directors resigned at closing, management participation/equity rollover was expressly not a condition, and only the CFO had a disclosed continuing role—yet continuing employees remained with the surviving corporation under a contractual benefits bridge, so processes did not transfer without an aligned people substrate; no TSA/operating-agreement gap fill was required or documented.
